### **Summary**

The team optimized k-fold training configurations and reviewed synthetic data experiments to improve overall model performance.

**Training Pipeline Infrastructure Optimization**  
The team reduced the repeat factor to 1 and increased epoch counts to optimize training efficiency. Parallelization strategies were implemented to improve hardware throughput across available compute resources.

**Synthetic Data Performance Analysis**  
Experiments with synthetic masks demonstrated improved object detection capabilities. Teams shifted focus toward confusion matrices to accurately communicate high-precision model performance to clients.

**Model Evaluation And Challenges**  
Evaluations identified model confusion between background noise and objects in complex datasets. Utilizing verified annotations is required to improve distinction between artifacts and background features.

### **Decisions**

## Aligned

* **Model evaluation window defined** The team will evaluate models after the first 10 epochs to determine the best performing architecture for further training.

* **Repeat factor and epoch counts set** The repeat factor is set to 1 and the total training epochs are set to 200 to optimize the training process.

* **Model training infrastructure and parallelization** V1 training is moved to Ninja, V4 training is moved to Volley/Blackwell, and all K-fold training jobs are set to run in parallel.

* **Customer reporting metrics format** The team will use confusion matrices as the primary performance reporting metric for the customer, rather than relying solely on F1 scores.

* **Test time scaling as optional feature** The team will present test time scaling as a performance option for the client if the signal is positive, rather than designating it as the primary shipping model.

* **Incorporating Treasure Island dataset** The model training strategy is updated to incorporate the Treasure Island dataset to address data distribution gaps regarding rocky backgrounds.

We've **updated the Decisions section** using your feedback.

### **Next steps**

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Analyze Training Time: Investigate why training models are taking longer than expected. Determine per-epoch time to calculate the optimal number of epochs and repeat factors.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Evaluate Models: Assess Fold 1 models to obtain object-based metrics. Evaluate base V4 cut and paste performance on the regular dataset.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Setup Pipeline: Configure the Blackwell pipeline for training runs. Start training runs on the remaining available GPUs.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Share Logs: Upload and share the log files and performance curves for long-running jobs.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Produce Evaluation Metrics: Create confusion matrices showing raw numbers and percentages for model evaluation. Generate model predictions and corresponding visualizations for all tested models.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Configure Experiments: Set up K-fold training for current models. Prepare a separate training experiment using only synthetically generated augmentations.

- [ ] \[The group\] Get Feedback: Execute the planned training and evaluation runs to obtain results by the weekend.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Run Blackwell Experiments: Run training experiments using the Blackwell platform to optimize performance and processing time. Ensure that training tasks are split appropriately to leverage available GPU resources.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Share Confusion Matrices: Send the generated confusion matrices to Hemanth and Geoff by Sunday to assist with final model assessment. Provide these results as soon as possible to ensure timely progress.

- [ ] \[Ratul Shashank\] Upload Code: Upload the experiment code to a dedicated branch in the Bedrock GitHub repository. Include documentation on the entry point and instructions for execution.

- [ ] \[Ratul Shashank\] Build Comparison App: Develop an application that allows users to compare real and synthetic examples side by side. Present a plan for deployment to the team for review.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh, Sachin Pandey\] Provide Weekend Updates: Provide project progress updates throughout the weekend to keep the team informed. Coordinate with the team on a call if necessary.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Prepare Metrics Report: Generate a clean report showing the two required metrics for the regular dataset to clarify confusion between model classes. Address the issues identified with previous iterations.

- [ ] \[Geoff Horowitz\] Analyze Software Source: Research the source of the software used for magnetic data analysis to understand the verification process. Communicate the findings regarding how the data was verified.

### **Details**

*Did the screenshots in this section make your notes [better](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5bXzKQfylMIhSXc?entryPoint=multimodal&isGoogler=False&isBetter=True&confid=lO2y5yU4uUQrdGJK016XDxIUOBEBMgUIigIgABgECA) or [worse](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5bXzKQfylMIhSXc?entryPoint=multimodal&isGoogler=False&isBetter=False&confid=lO2y5yU4uUQrdGJK016XDxIUOBEBMgUIigIgABgECA)?*

* **K-Fold Training Status**: Sachin provided an update on the k-fold data, confirming that they fixed and verified the data by checking pixel counts and ensuring no overlap between original and cropped data. Sachin noted that training for three models—Base V4, B4 with heavy augmentation, and B4 with augmentation plus cut and paste—has been running for approximately 17 hours on fold one ([00:01:08](#00:01:08)). Geoff questioned the extended duration, as previous estimates for such runs were around eight hours ([00:04:12](#00:04:12)).

* **Training Efficiency vs. Accuracy**: The team discussed the discrepancy in training time, with Sachin attributing the increase to the removal of early stopping, which previously halted training after 25 epochs but is now extending to 76 epochs ([00:05:38](#00:05:38)). Hemanth questioned whether the models were performing well, and Sachin confirmed that accuracy remains stable with an IOU between 50% and 60%, clarifying that the issue is a performance bottleneck rather than a lack of model accuracy ([00:07:14](#00:07:14)).

* **Evaluation and Monitoring**: Sachin plans to evaluate the completed fold one models to generate object-based metrics and verify the base V4 cut-and-paste model on the regular dataset ([00:10:22](#00:10:22)). Hemanth requested that Sachin provide training curves for the jobs and explain the specific early stopping criteria, which is currently set to 60 epochs ([00:11:39](#00:11:39)).

* **Hardware and Capacity**: The team analyzed the current infrastructure, noting that the epoch duration is roughly 13 to 14 minutes, which results in a 15-hour training time if early stopping is triggered at 60 epochs ([00:13:37](#00:13:37)). Pratyaksh and Hemanth discussed the potential of utilizing the Blackwell GPU architecture, which supports splitting tasks across more units to increase throughput ([00:19:03](#00:19:03)) ([00:28:24](#00:28:24)).

  ![][image1]

* **Repeat Factor Optimization**: Pratyaksh explained that the "repeat factor" was originally implemented to ensure adequate random crops for smaller datasets. After discussion, Pratyaksh and Sachin agreed to reduce the repeat factor to 1 to avoid redundant processing, and they discussed increasing the epoch count to 200 or 300 to compensate ([00:20:35](#00:20:35)) ([00:23:16](#00:23:16)).

  ![][image2]

* **Training Pipeline and Contention**: Pratyaksh proposed capping training at 20 hours to allow for more efficient model selection ([00:25:44](#00:25:44)). Hemanth and Pratyaksh also discussed potential CPU bottlenecks caused by OpenCV and NumPy in the multi-processing pipeline, suggesting they could limit worker counts to reduce memory contention ([00:30:03](#00:30:03)).

* **Model Allocation Strategy**: The team established a plan to optimize resources by shifting V1 training to the Ninja machine and running the heavy B4 models on Volley ([00:38:47](#00:38:47)). They decided to run all folds in parallel, with Pratyaksh offering to provide implementation code for tracking objects missed during the training loop ([00:40:30](#00:40:30)).

* **Synthetic Data and Architecture Updates**: Pratyaksh shared updates on their synthetic data experiment, noting a transition from single-channel grayscale input to a three-channel setup using pre-trained ImageNet weights ([00:42:04](#00:42:04)). Early results indicate that "poison copy paste" combined with "procedural mine" augmentation significantly improves performance, with some instances missing only one or two objects ([00:45:58](#00:45:58)) ([00:50:03](#00:50:03)).

  ![][image3]

* **Evaluation Metrics and Communication**: Pratyaksh noted that while the current setup shows high recall, the F1 score is around 67% due to aggressive predictions ([00:47:06](#00:47:06)). Hemanth emphasized that to satisfy customers who expect high accuracy, the team must use confusion matrices—presenting both raw numbers and percentages—to clearly articulate model performance ([00:51:19](#00:51:19)).

  ![][image4]

* **Next Steps and Timeline**: The team agreed to integrate these experiments into the k-fold workflow to facilitate direct comparisons ([00:54:50](#00:54:50)). Pratyaksh committed to parallelizing the k-fold experiments on available GPUs with a 24-hour turnaround target. The goal is to identify the top one or two models by the next meeting on Monday, which will then proceed to final training ([00:57:08](#00:57:08)).

  ![][image5]

* **Inference Strategy and Resource Budgeting**: Pratyaksh Singh proposed running multiple models during inference or applying destructive data augmentations to improve precision and reduce overfitting, noting that they could provide confidence metrics for different augmentations ([01:00:28](#01:00:28)). Geoff Horowitz indicated that while they have the time budget to test these approaches, they do not have the compute budget for parallel execution, meaning any multi-model strategy would have to be run in series ([00:59:12](#00:59:12)). The team discussed utilizing "test-time scaling," similar to OpenAI's approach, where increased time leads to better recall, provided the performance signal justifies the cost ([01:01:43](#01:01:43)). They agreed to test this concept but decided not to commit to shipping it unless the testing phase demonstrates clear performance improvements ([01:02:59](#01:02:59)).

  ![][image6]

* **Project Deadlines and Training Focus**: Hemanth Sarabu requested that the team push to finalize the model by Monday, with an interim goal of sharing confusion matrices by Sunday to provide visibility to the group. Hemanth Sarabu emphasized that the team should prioritize generative and synthetic data approaches rather than spending excessive time training ResNet models, as those methods are more interesting and potentially higher performing ([01:05:31](#01:05:31)).

  ![][image7]

* **Object Masking and Data Synthesis Experiments**: Ratul Shashank provided an update on experimenting with new object shapes by manipulating metrics such as brightness, contrast, and shape ([01:06:32](#01:06:32)). By increasing the standard deviation threshold for dark and bright pixels from 0.5 to 1.5, Ratul Shashank was able to create experimental masks that allow for the elongation or bulging of objects along specific axes to simulate different light directions, moving away from rigid primitives like circles or water drops. The current open challenge for this task is determining the specific extent of modification that can be applied to objects ([01:08:39](#01:08:39)) ([01:12:51](#01:12:51)).

  ![][image8]

* **Code Accessibility and Client Presentation**: To facilitate collaboration, Ratul Shashank agreed to push the current code to a new branch on the Bedrock GitHub repository, including necessary documentation for the entry point. Additionally, Geoff Horowitz requested that an application be created to compare real and synthetic examples, which would allow the client to review the data and make selections ([01:14:16](#01:14:16)).

* **Model Evaluation and Metric Analysis**: Sachin Pandey reported on the training of the V4 AG model on the "Wall-E" dataset. Sachin Pandey acknowledged that a previously reported 90+ F1 score was inaccurate because the model conflated "AOI big" and "black patch" classes, artificially inflating the results ([01:17:08](#01:17:08)). To resolve this, Sachin Pandey plans to generate a clean report with two specific metrics to clarify performance and is considering adjusting the learning rate, as the model training stopped around 50 epochs ([01:22:15](#01:22:15)) ([01:26:36](#01:26:36)).

  ![][image9]

* **Treasure Island Dataset and Feature Distribution**: The team reviewed the V4 M3 model's predictions on the Treasure Island dataset, observing that while the model successfully identifies some UXOs, it struggles with backgrounds ([01:27:55](#01:27:55)) ([01:31:57](#01:31:57)). Sachin Pandey explained that the rocky backgrounds in the Treasure Island data are underrepresented in the current training set and share features with UXOs, such as shadows, curves, and bumps, which leads to model confusion ([01:32:56](#01:32:56)). The team discussed leveraging Bedrock's verified and unverified annotations to improve the model's confidence in distinguishing between actual contacts and background noise ([01:29:19](#01:29:19)) ([01:35:58](#01:35:58)).

  ![][image10]

* **Technical Infrastructure Setup**: Geoff Horowitz confirmed that the Jetson setup is complete for Sachin Pandey, utilizing the username "cresser" to maintain path consistency with other bedrock platforms ([01:37:45](#01:37:45)).
